markdown_report:
The strongest next step is a **terminal-mask supervision pilot** within the corrected BERT4Rec baseline. At 20% research progress, it offers a smaller, directly testable intervention than expanding activation localization.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have measured negative-wins rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These training-pair measurements identify weaker separation but do not establish validation performance. (2) Alignment scores near 0.51 correspond to mean embedding cosines near zero. They provide little support for treating directional collapse as the primary problem. (3) Existing serving-parity gates and disjoint-user patch confirmation support controlled diagnosis. Patching effects nevertheless depend on the chosen intervention and cannot establish users’ current needs.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already includes last-item masking. This motivates testing its allocation of supervision rather than claiming a new masking principle. (2) [Zhang and Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) show that corruption choices and metrics affect activation localization. Preserve the bounded patching pilot as supporting evidence, without using localization alone to select training changes. (3) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939) identifies loss-related overconfidence in sequential recommendation. Hold loss and sampling fixed initially so the pilot isolates masking allocation.

**Framework and directions.** Organize the work along three axes:

| Direction | Evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Objective alignment | Matched interior/terminal training-prefix ranks | Whether serving-task supervision improves validation |
| History dependence | Recent/older perturbations and residual patches | Whether dependence is useful |
| Evidence sufficiency | Public titles, descriptions, timestamps | Compatibility and current intent often remain unknown |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores below are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Terminal-mask mixture: 3/7/3.** Originality: established technique, but a focused task-specific test. Potential: directly addresses an objective mismatch, though gains are uncertain. Difficulty: small sampler change, with careful leakage checks required.
- **Matched interior-versus-terminal audit: 4/6/4.** Originality: useful controlled comparison, but conventional paired evaluation. Potential: separates reconstruction from serving behavior, without itself improving recommendations. Difficulty: reuses interfaces, but needs matched targets and user-level uncertainty.
- **Bidirectional patch confirmation: 5/6/6.** Originality: recommender-specific restoration/disruption controls, derived from existing patching. Potential: localizes intervention effects, with limited semantic interpretation. Difficulty: frozen-model hooks are feasible, but donor matching and multiplicity complicate implementation.

**Selected algorithm.** Replace a fixed fraction of ordinary masked-reconstruction examples with training-prefix terminal-mask examples. Start with one preregistered mixture probability, 0.5, and compare against the supplied baseline using unchanged host macro validation HR@10. This tests an objective mismatch; it does not encode compatibility or prove recent intent.

```text
sample a training-only history endpoint t
with probability 0.5:
    input = left_pad(history[:t][-maxlen+1:] + [MASK])
    supervise only MASK with history[t]
otherwise:
    use corrected baseline masked-target sampler
optimize unchanged baseline loss
```

Keep seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Retain one checkpoint per category, routing, diagnostic contracts, final-nonpadding readout, and matching embedded predictor code. Report actual validation results only after host evaluation.

idea.description: Test a 0.5 mixture of terminal-mask training-prefix examples and the corrected BERT4Rec baseline’s masked-reconstruction examples, retaining one independently trained model per category.
idea.motivation: Interior reconstruction can use right context unavailable during appended-mask inference. Increasing terminal-mask supervision is a feasible early-stage hypothesis, supported by BERT4Rec’s existing last-item masking design; the supplied diagnostics do not establish that this change will improve validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Change only training-example allocation for the initial pilot; preserve the baseline architecture, loss, negative sampling and optimizer. Draw endpoints exclusively from training histories. On terminal examples, exclude the selected target occurrence and every later interaction, retain the latest maxlen−1 preceding items, append the reserved MASK, and left-pad. Supervise only masked positions. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and batches per epoch 200. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four category routes, and exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Keep predictor-writer architecture and checkpoint loading consistent. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and ModelView compatibility. Read the final nonpadding MASK position. Treat patching and paired training-prefix diagnostics as supporting measurements; select using the unchanged host macro validation HR@10. No validation gain has been measured for this proposal.
idea.pseudocode:
set preprocessing_seed=0 and training_seed=42
for each of the four supplied categories:
    initialize corrected BERT4Rec baseline
    for epoch in range(at_most_200):
        for batch in range(200):
            examples = []
            for sampled training history:
                if seeded_random() < 0.5:
                    choose eligible training endpoint t with nonempty preceding context
                    target = history[t]
                    tokens = history[:t][-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK]
                    sequence = left_pad(tokens, maxlen)
                    labels = IGNORE everywhere except final MASK, labeled target
                    sample negatives using unchanged baseline policy
                else:
                    sequence, labels, negatives = corrected_baseline_masked_example(history)
                assert every supervised input position contains reserved MASK
                examples.append(sequence, labels, negatives)
            update using unchanged baseline loss and optimizer
    export one selected category checkpoint and its compatible predictor
run unchanged host validation; compare four-category macro HR@10

originality.positive: Turns the diagnosed serving mismatch into a narrow, controlled experiment within the required BERT4Rec family.
originality.negative: Terminal masking is already part of BERT4Rec; this is an allocation study rather than a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: Could establish whether serving-aligned supervision is a productive direction before spending budget on more complex interventions.
future_potential.negative: It may not improve validation and does not directly resolve compatibility, duplication or unobserved current intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a localized sampler change and leaves inference architecture unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct endpoint selection, masked-only labels, left padding and diagnostic compatibility still require careful verification.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Includes last-item masking, providing direct precedent for terminal-supervision allocation.
limitations: Does not establish which masking allocation is best for these four fixed RecHarness datasets.
Reconstruction performance alone does not establish appended-mask validation ranking quality.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Shows that corruption methods and evaluation metrics affect activation-patching conclusions.
Supports controlled interventions and explicit score-based measurements.
limitations: Provides no direct evidence that recommender patching predicts validation improvements.
Intervention effects do not establish natural semantic pathways or user intent.

related_work.title: gSASRec study of overconfidence in sequential recommendation
contributions: Investigates overconfidence associated with sampled binary cross-entropy in sequential recommendation.
Motivates treating optimization and sampling as possible confounders.
limitations: Its architecture and objective findings do not directly establish behavior in the supplied BERT4Rec baseline.
Does not demonstrate that terminal-mask reallocation improves this benchmark.
